questions.question: In which of the following cases did the Supreme Court direct that, 'the Parliament cannot take away or abridge any of the fundamental rights for the Implementation of Directive Principles'?
questions.solution:
In the Golak Nath Case (1967), the Supreme Court ruled that Fundamental Rights (FRs) are 'sacrosanct' and the Parliament cannot take away or abridge them, even for the implementation of Directive Principles.
  • Significance: This led to a major confrontation between the Judiciary and Executive, eventually resulting in the 24th Amendment Act.

questions.question: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts made the president bound by the advice of the council of ministers headed by the prime minister?
questions.solution:
The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 made the President bound by the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.
  • Article 74: Before this, the language was slightly ambiguous. The 44th Amendment later added a proviso that the President can send the advice back once for reconsideration, but must follow it if sent again.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT the qualification for the appointment of judges of supreme court?
questions.option_1: A judge of high court for at least five years
questions.option_2: An advocate of supreme court for at least ten years
questions.option_3: An advocate of high court for at least ten years
questions.option_4: A distinguished judge in the opinion of the President
questions.solution:
The requirement to be 'An advocate of the Supreme Court for at least ten years' is NOT a qualification for an SC judge.
  • Correct Qualifications: 1. Citizen of India. 2. Judge of a High Court for 5 years. 3. Advocate of a High Court (not SC) for 10 years. 4. A distinguished jurist in the opinion of the President.

questions.question: In which of the following cases did the Supreme court of India give a ruling that, 'in case of any conflict between the fundamental rights and the directive principles, the former would prevail'?
questions.solution:
In the Champakam Dorairajan Case (1951), the Supreme Court first ruled that in case of conflict, Fundamental Rights would prevail over Directive Principles.
  • Subsidiary Status: The Court held that DPSPs have to run as a 'subsidiary' to Fundamental Rights.
  • Evolution: This stance shifted significantly over the years through the Minerva Mills case, which established a 'harmony and balance' between the two.

questions.question: Who among the following was the President of India when India launched its first Nuclear test in Pokhran?
questions.solution:
V.V. Giri was the President of India when the first nuclear test, Smiling Buddha, was conducted in Pokhran in May 1974.
  • Prime Minister: Indira Gandhi was the PM during this test.
  • Note: Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam was the President during much later years, though he was the chief scientist during the 1998 (Pokhran-II) tests.
